title: Fin Box Rib Web — Doubler Repair at the Lower Attachment Bay
abstract: Doubler repair for a crack or a corrosion clean-up in the fin box rib web at the lower attachment bay, done in situ with the fin on the aircraft.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the shear capability of the fin box rib web at the lower attachment bay after a crack has been stopped or after corrosion has been blended out.
sections.damage_assessment: Establish the extent of the damage by detailed visual inspection and eddy current inspection of the whole web bay. This repair is valid for a single stopped crack up to 45 mm long, or for a corrosion blend-out no deeper than fifteen per cent of the web thickness over an area up to 100 mm by 100 mm. Damage that reaches the rib flange, damage in the fastener row that attaches the web to the attachment fitting, and any damage in the adjacent bay are outside the scope. Record the bay number and the position relative to the rib flange, because the doubler orientation depends on it.
sections.repair_procedure: Get access to the bay from inside the fin through the access panels, with the fin box lighting rigged. Clean the web and confirm the damage map. Where a crack is present, drill and ream a stop hole at each tip and do a dye penetrant inspection of both holes. Cut the doubler from sheet to the layout of the repair drawing, dress the edges and check the fit against the web with the doubler held dry. Drill the fastener pattern into the web D5530118601329 using the doubler as a template, keeping the pattern clear of the existing fastener rows by the distance on the drawing. Deburr every hole and apply the surface protection of the standard practice. Install the doubler wet with sealant using anchor nuts AES147323-7D at the positions shown, and solid fasteners elsewhere. Where the doubler footprint reaches the angle D5530112998387, transfer the pattern into it rather than stopping the doubler short. Restore the sealant fillet along the doubler edge.
sections.inspection_requirements: This repair is life limited to 20 000 flight cycles from embodiment. Do a repeat eddy current inspection of the doubler perimeter and of any stop hole every 5 000 flight cycles. Report the repair to Aeralis with the bay number and the damage map. A second repair in the same bay is not permitted; the rib must be replaced instead.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: One stopped crack up to 45 mm, or a corrosion blend-out no deeper than fifteen per cent of web thickness over 100 mm by 100 mm, clear of the rib flange and of the attachment fastener row.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Two staggered rows, 28 fasteners, 22 mm pitch, 15 mm edge distance
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Life limited to 20 000 flight cycles; repeat eddy current inspection of the doubler perimeter every 5 000 flight cycles.

issue.reason: Deliberate decision not to read the wing cover fastener standard across to this scheme recorded in the design justification.

Read-across note: this scheme was reviewed against the cold-worked interference-fit fastener standard of MOD-161688 during the pre-analysis of that change and no read-across applies. The wording of the two schemes is close — both speak of a doubler, a stopped crack, an edge distance and a wet-installed perimeter — but the fin box rib web uses its own anchor nut family and its own hole preparation, the web is metallic rather than laminate, and nothing in the wing cover substantiation reaches it. The decision is recorded here so that the same comparison is not made again at the next revision of either scheme.
